clue.text: Pull the plug

definitions.meaning: to pull on a cigarette or pipe is to draw on it in short breaths
to plug a product is to give it a promotional write-up or boost

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a drag on a cigarette, and an exaggerated bit of publicity praising something.

clue.text: Goalposts are widely separated

parts.note: the uprights at either end of a pitch stand far from each other, and the phrase for those posts also means utterly different

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means as far apart as the earth's two ends, here pictured as uprights at opposite ends of a field.

clue.text: Garland moulded of stone

indicators.note: moulded suggests material shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A decorative wreath carved out of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A festoon is a chain of flowers or ribbons hung in a curve, a garland.

clue.text: Cloths originally made under inflexible rules for Scottish baron

parts.note: tweeds are rough woollen cloths, originally from the Scottish Borders

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A Scottish nobleman whose woollens were first woven under a strict regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the initial letters of 'made under inflexible rules', giving MUIR to follow TWEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: John Buchan, the novelist and Governor General of Canada, was created the first Baron of this title, a Scottish peerage.

clue.text: Small man finds time to sleep after work

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
a man in chess is a piece, such as a knight

explanation.surface: A little fellow finds time for rest after his shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' means a chess piece, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeknight is an evening between Monday and Friday, when one sleeps before another working day.

clue.text: Two notes summed up character

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the combined letters from bottom to top

parts.note: soh is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A pair of written messages captured someone's personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summed' joins the two notes SOH and TE into SOHTE; 'up' turns that upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the distinctive character or spirit of a person, group or culture.

clue.text: Out of stupidity, left with a lot of confusing directions — west is not one

indicators.note: confusing jumbles the many compass letters and the letter for left

parts.note: the compass points N, E and S supply these letters, with W excluded

explanation.surface: Muddled travel directions lead to sheer foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of directions' gives six S, four E and two N; 'west is not one' rules out W. 'confusing' mixes them with L.
explanation.definitionFit: Senselessness is the lack of good sense, foolishness or stupidity.

clue.text: Peace-keepers encounter a snag, resulting in divorce?

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peace-keeping forces
a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: Peace-keepers hit a problem that ends a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: to get hitched is to marry, so to undo the knot is to divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is slang for marrying, so unfastening the hitch playfully means splitting up.

clue.text: Fairground entertainment free to R leader of excursion

parts.note: to rid is to free

indicators.note: leader of asks for the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A free fairground attraction to start an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is an amusement such as a big wheel or roller coaster at a funfair.

clue.text: Sheets are drooping in vessels' stretch of water

indicators.note: in puts the drooping word inside the shipping route

parts.note: a shipping lane is a route across the sea that ships follow
to sag is to droop

explanation.surface: Sails hang limp as ships pass through a channel.
explanation.definitionFit: This pasta comes in broad flat sheets layered in the baked dish.

clue.text: Roger understood

definitions.meaning: in radio talk, roger signals that a message has been received
grasped the meaning of what was said

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the radio reply confirming receipt, and the idiom for grasping what was meant.

clue.text: Henry, hit, powerless, bent over

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: less takes the letter for power away from the word before it

parts.note: punched means hit
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A man named Henry, struck and weakened, doubles over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' splits into 'power' (P) and 'less', removing it from PUNCHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hunched has their back curved forward, stooping as though bent over.

clue.text: Way of writing that's not hard — running smoothly, pleasantly brief

indicators.note: not removes the letter for hard from the writing system

parts.note: shorthand is a system of rapid writing using symbols
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an engine running sweet is working without trouble

explanation.surface: A style of writing that is easy, fluent and agreeably concise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' drops one H from SHORTHAND, leaving SHORTAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something brief and agreeable, especially a short speech or visit.

clue.text: Puts up with daring leader going astray Check to — that's amazing

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top
the leading letter of the word for daring wanders off and is lost

parts.note: defying means daring or challenging

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a bold leader who has lost the way, astonishingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PUTS into STUP; 'leader going astray' drops D from DEFYING, leaving EFYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupefying means astounding, so overwhelming that it leaves one dazed.

clue.text: A little appropriate

definitions.meaning: a small amount, as of salt held between finger and thumb
used as a verb, to appropriate is to take or steal something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tiny quantity of seasoning and, informally, to steal.

clue.text: Describing ammunition, got phrase wrong

indicators.note: wrong tells us the letters of the two words are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A commentator mislabels a type of artillery round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is a link word here, introducing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cannon load of small iron balls packed together like a bunch of fruit.

clue.text: Roads in Alaska

definitions.meaning: roads, or roadsteads, are sheltered waters where ships can lie at anchor
a place in Alaska, its largest city

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a place for ships to anchor, like a roadstead, and the name of Alaska's biggest city.

clue.text: Two chambers said to be suffering from disorder

indicators.note: said tells us the two words are spoken, giving something that sounds alike

parts.note: a room and an attic are two chambers of a house

explanation.surface: Two rooms are rumoured to be in a state of chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: ROOM plus ATTIC, spoken together, sounds like a word for a sufferer from joint pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheumatic person suffers from rheumatism, a disorder of the joints and muscles.

clue.text: Love to impress me, when lifting prohibition

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue raises the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to grab someone is to impress them

explanation.surface: A suitor tries to impress while a ban is being lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' reverses O GRAB ME in this down entry; 'to' and 'when' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade with a country.

clue.text: In flood, proceeded through the water quietly

parts.note: swam means moved through water by swimming
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: In a flood, someone swam silently through the waters.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp something is to flood or overwhelm it with water.

clue.text: Engrave with incorrect spelling? Fury results

indicators.note: with incorrect spelling tells us the letters are written out in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A badly spelt inscription causes anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fury' is not anger but one of the Furies, the avenging goddesses of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies of Greek myth pursued wrongdoers as spirits of vengeance.

clue.text: Distraught as well, having eaten a single brownie

indicators.note: having eaten places the word for single inside the word for as well

parts.note: besides means as well or in addition
one means a single
a brownie is a household sprite of folklore, a kind of elf

explanation.surface: Upset as well after eating one chocolate cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brownie' is not the cake but the helpful goblin of Scottish folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means frantic with worry or emotion, out of one's mind.

clue.text: Do likewise?

parts.note: 'do' is the written short form of a word meaning the same again, so do here stands for likewise

explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation do is used in lists to mean the same as above, likewise.

clue.text: As a star, I do likewise, at least to start with

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to start with asks for the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Being famous, I copy others, at least at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a celebrated star adored by fans.

clue.text: Lethargic porter, short on oxygen, beginning to twitch

indicators.note: short on means lacking one O for oxygen

parts.note: a doorman is a porter at a building's entrance
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A sluggish doorkeeper, breathless, starts to show signs of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short on oxygen' removes one O from DOORMAN, leaving DORMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or asleep, close to sluggish and lethargic.

clue.text: Charlie, for instance, has excellent weapon

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool, as is an ass
eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance
A1 is first-class, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A person called Charlie owns a fine weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is not a name but British slang for a fool: 'a right charlie'. A1 (first-rate) is read as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Stable, but having casual fights

parts.note: loose can mean casual or relaxed
boxes means fights with the fists

explanation.surface: Steady, despite having occasional scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: A loosebox is a stall in a stable where a horse can move about untethered.

clue.text: Strait-laced chap relaxes grip

indicators.note: relaxes signals the letters of the word that follows are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: A stiff, puritanical man loosens his hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A prig is a self-righteously proper person, smugly strict about morals.
